simple.meaning: יָבַם (yâbam) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to marry a (deceased) brother's widow.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Genesis, Deuteronomy, beginning at Genesis 38:8. Its contexts include family, family line, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָבַם (H2992).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: יָבַם (yâbam) / H2992 is traced through Genesis 38:8, Deuteronomy 25:5, Deuteronomy 25:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: perform the duty of a husband's brother, marry.
definitions.full: H2992. yabam [ יָבַם ] verb denominative , only Pi`el do the duty of יָבָם to a brother's widow; Perfect וְיִבְּמָהּ consecutive Deut 25:5 and shall do a brother-in-law's office to her; Imperative אֹתָהּ יַבֵּם Gen 38:8 (i.e. אָחִיךָ אֵשֶׁת v a ); Infinitive suffix יַבְּמִי אָבָה לֹא Deut 25:7 (on nominal suffix as object of infinitive, see Ges § 115 R. 2 near the end). יִבְנִיָּה יִבְנְיָה, יַבְנֶה, יַבְנְאֵל, see below בנה . יַבֹּק see below בקק above יְבֶרֶכְיָ֫הוּ see below ברך above יִבְשָׂם see below בשׂם above

occurrences.englishText: Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.”

If brothers dwell together, and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, and take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her.

If the man doesn’t want to take his brother’s wife, then his brother’s wife shall go up to the gate to the elders, and say, “My husband’s brother refuses to raise up to his brother a name in Israel. He will not perform the duty of a husband’s brother to me.”
